---
title: "Day 1 · Understanding data and making comparisons"
---

Two hours of theory followed by two hours of guided practical work in R.

## Learning objectives

By the end of Day 1 you will be able to:

- Describe a dataset in terms of observations, variables and variable types
- Check a dataset for missing values, impossible values and coding problems
- Choose and calculate suitable summaries: counts, proportions, mean (SD), median (IQR)
- Choose a suitable plot: bar chart, histogram or boxplot
- Explain what a confidence interval and a p-value do and do not tell you
- Compare two or more groups with a t-test, ANOVA or a rank-based test, and say why
- Analyse a contingency table and explain proportions, risks, odds, RR and OR
- Recognise paired data and avoid analysing it as independent groups

## Theory sessions

| Part | Topic | Minutes |
|:--|:--|:--:|
| 1 | Questions, observations, variables, data quality | 20 |
| 2 | Describing data: summaries and plots | 25 |
| 3 | From a sample to a population: variability, effect sizes, CIs, tests | 25 |
| 4 | Comparing groups: continuous outcomes, paired data | 22 |
| 5 | Associations between categorical variables; first look at confounding | 18 |

<iframe src="../../downloads/slides/Day1_Understanding_data_and_comparisons.pdf" width="100%" height="560" style="border: 1px solid #EAF2F5;" title="Day 1 slides"></iframe>

::: {.key-findings}
**Key messages of Day 1.** Start from the question, the outcome type and the design (independent or paired). Describe the data before testing. Report an effect size with a 95% confidence interval; a p-value alone is not enough. Proportions, risks and odds differ, and the study design decides which you can interpret.
:::
